thread:
maya: quick q — for the lightweight surface we sketched for hosted/dedicated/private, how do we want to handle auth propagation in sidecarless private mode?
Tony: are you talking about the case where customer's control plane runs in their VPC and we don't have a sidecar to rebind secrets?
maya: yes. customers want private control plane + runtime; no sidecar allowed in their policy.
Olga: two options i keep coming back to: 1) short-lived delegated tokens issued by control plane to runtime (token exchange), or 2) runtime fetches secrets from a customer KMS via a proxy we provide.
Liam: token exchange seems cleaner for us (less network surface) but it's tricky for air-gapped on-prem where control plane can't reach runtime.
Tony: right. for on-prem we probably need a pull model (runtime->customer-kms) or a manual secret injection step at deploy.
maya: what about a hybrid: default token exchange for hosted/dedicated, but expose a fallback "kms-pull" adapter for private/on-prem with a configurable polling cadence?
Olga: i worry about poll cadence and perf — polling KMS every request is no-go. need a cache + rotation strategy and clear TTL semantics.
Liam: agree. propose: adapter does initial fetch, caches locally with TTL, and control plane can push rotation hooks via a signed webhook when available.
Tony: sounds reasonable. also need to standardize error semantics across modes: FAIL_OPEN vs FAIL_CLOSED for auth failures. customers will want determinism.
maya: can we default to FAIL_CLOSED for private, FAIL_OPEN for hosted (with telemetry + alerting)?
Olga: yes, but call that out in the surface docs. and we must include a clear circuit-breaker: after N auth errors within T, runtime should stop attempts and return 503 with a structured error code.
Liam: agree. sample error shape: `{code: "AUTH_PROXY_UNAVAILABLE", mode: "private"}` — but we'll publish exact schema.
maya: small config example for fallback so we can review later:
```
auth:
  mode: hybrid         # token-exchange | kms-pull | hybrid
  cache_ttl: 5m
  fail_policy: closed # open | closed
  rotation_webhook: https://hooks.customer.internal/rotate
```
Tony: nice. two operational notes: 1) telemetry — we need per-tenant token-exchange metrics (+latency + failure_rate) surfaced in console. 2) RBAC — who can flip fail_policy? only org-admins.
Olga: + add audit log events for rotation_webhook invocations and token issuance.
maya: action items: 1) olga + liam to draft minimal adapter API (kms-pull contract + cache semantics) by EOD Friday, 2) tony to draft telemetry/alerting KPIs and default thresholds, 3) i'll update the hosting surface doc to call out FAIL_OPEN/CLOSED defaults and examples.
Liam: ack. i'll include a short state machine for cache lifecycle (fresh -> expiring -> refresh_in_progress -> stale).
infra-bot: deploy-check: no blocking issues found for the sketch. :white_check_mark:
Tony: thanks. if anyone sees a huge gap call it out here, otherwise we'll sync briefly on Monday in arch sync. :thumbsup:
